headline: AI-capex doubts after Tesla/Meta, chips hit (Lam −7–8%), Brent ~$112: NQ −1.6% pre-open, gap below Wednesday's low. Sell failed bounces.
session_note: Cash open 9:30 AM ET (10:30 AM Atlantic) · morning window

flip.long: NDX gets back above Tuesday's close (29,490; NQ ≈ 29,675) and then Wednesday's low (29,594; NQ ≈ 29,780) and holds after 9:30, with the 10-year staying near/below ~5.05%.
flip.short: Confirmation: NQ breaks the overnight low (29,417; ≈ NDX 29,232) in the first 30 min. Next target is Tuesday's NDX low (29,209), and Friday's 29,188 close below that.

thesis: Wednesday's AI rally is unwinding. Nasdaq-100 futures were ~29,524–29,533 at 8:40–8:42 AM ET, down ~1.6% (−475 to −485 pts) from Wednesday's 30,007 settle, after an overnight low of 29,417 [1,2]. Megacap earnings didn't help. Tesla is −3–5% after cutting 2026 capex to ~$20B, and Meta is −1–2% despite a revenue beat because it raised capex and is issuing new non-voting shares [3,4,5]. Lam Research is −7–8% on in-line guidance, and Intel, AMD, Qualcomm, Broadcom, Micron, CoreWeave and Nebius are down 3–5%+ [3,4,6]. IBM is −5% after its CEO said customers are questioning AI returns [4,5]. Brent is ~$111.75 (+2.7%) on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and the US ordering staff out [1,6]. The one offset is a flight to safety: the 10-year is ~5.04% vs 5.15% Wednesday (≈ −11 bp) [7]. Jobless claims were strong at **194K vs 200K expected** but didn't move the tape [8]. The Fed is in blackout (Oct 28 hike ~14–17%, Dec hike ~84% cumulative) [9,10]. Futures imply an NDX open near ~29,350, below Tuesday's 29,490 close and Wednesday's 29,594 low [2,11]. The 9:30 edge is **with the selling**: short failed bounces below Tuesday's close. Conviction is low because the gap is already large and falling yields could fuel a reflex bounce.

bullets.label: Fresh megacap catalysts point down.
bullets.text: Tesla beat on EPS ($0.48 vs ~$0.43) but cut 2026 capex to ~$20B from >$25B and pushed meaningful robotaxi revenue out to 2027–28. Meta beat on revenue ($64.6B vs $63.3–63.4B) but raised capex to $135–145B and added a non-voting share class, and it reversed to −1–2% premarket [3,4,5].

bullets.label: Chips and AI infra lead the selling.
bullets.text: Lam Research is −7–8.4% on in-line Dec-quarter guidance. Intel is −4.4%, and AMD, Qualcomm, Marvell, Broadcom and Micron are −3% to −4.7%. Nvidia is −1.9%, CoreWeave/Nebius are −5%+, and IBM is −5% [3,4,5,6]. Asia was weak too (Nikkei −2.65%, CSI 300 in a bear market), and the Euro Stoxx 50 is −1.3% [1,6].

bullets.label: Gap opens below Wednesday's range.
bullets.text: NQ settled ~185 points over cash NDX Wednesday (30,007 vs 29,822.52). On that basis ~29,530 NQ implies an NDX open near 29,350, below Wednesday's 29,594 low and Tuesday's 29,490 close. That erases most of the week's 2.2% gain [2,6,11]. This is an approximate basis estimate, not a quote.

bullets.label: Data is out and was a non-event.
bullets.text: Initial claims came in at 194K vs 200K consensus (prior 200K). That's near 57-year lows: hawkish-leaning, but it didn't move futures [8,12]. Still to come: the Leading Index at 10:00 AM and the KC Fed manufacturing survey at 11:00 AM. There are no Fed speakers (blackout through Oct 29) [13].

bullets.label: Bull case:
bullets.text: This is a big gap (−1.6%) into a flight-to-safety bond rally. The 10-year is down ~11 bp to ~5.04%, the dollar is flat, and December hike odds haven't risen. Tesla and Meta both actually beat, Jensen Huang says neocloud demand is 'off the charts', and NQ is ~110 points off its overnight low. Large opening gaps after a strong prior day often see an early reflex bounce toward the prior close [4,5,6,7,9].

bullets.label: Bear case:
bullets.text: The market is punishing capex even on beats (Meta, Lam), and there's no tech-earnings catalyst until Microsoft/Alphabet next week. Brent is above $111 with Saudi/Iran escalation risk, which keeps the inflation and December-hike story alive. Breaking the overnight low opens a path to Tuesday's 29,209 low and Friday's 29,188 close [1,6,11].

bullets.label: Flip to LONG:
bullets.text: NDX reclaims Tuesday's close (29,490; NQ ≈ 29,675): stand aside. If it also gets above Wednesday's low (29,594; NQ ≈ 29,780) and holds through the first 30 min, with SMH turning up and the 10-year staying near/below 5.05%: go long.

bullets.label: Strengthen SHORT:
bullets.text: NQ breaks the overnight low (29,417; ≈ NDX 29,232) in the first 30 minutes, especially if Brent pushes above ~$112.5 or the 10-year bounces back above ~5.10%.

bullets.label: Wildcards:
bullets.text: The 10:00 AM Leading Index, Middle East/Saudi headlines, Tesla–SpaceX merger news, AI-financing/neocloud credit headlines, and any Warsh/Fed leak despite the blackout [1,3,13].

data_notes: The NQ quotes are indicative (Markets Insider is from market makers; Yahoo may be delayed ~10 min). The overnight range is from Yahoo's daily bar as of 8:31 AM ET and may have changed since. The NDX open implied from the ~185-pt futures premium is an estimate. The 10-year prints disagree: Yahoo ^TNX shows 5.04 vs a 5.15 prior close (−11 bp), Reuters had ~5.065% at ~7:10 AM, and Bloomberg had 5.08% (−4 bp) early in the European morning. So the size of the drop depends on which prior close you use. The DXY is roughly flat per Yahoo, while Bloomberg's dollar index was 'little changed'. The claims consensus is 200K (Reuters poll / Investing.com). I didn't find a consensus for the 10:00 AM Leading Index. No US Fed speakers today (blackout). No Nasdaq-100 megacap reports today before the open beyond the overnight Tesla/Meta/Lam/IBM results; after the close, Western Digital reports. Wednesday's NDX H/L/C were verified against Yahoo daily data.
